attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own newsletter, stated firmly and endorsed.

semantics.note: 'Have to be' states a requirement, not a prediction. Treating it as a conditional with the implied antecedent (sustaining commitments) matches the context. The horizon, 'roughly 2x per year', is preserved.

contract.note: Reading business size as revenue fits the surrounding revenue discussion. Testing whether a shortfall actually prevents the commitments from being funded is fair to the necessity claim. Tolerance and accounting basis are unspecified, as the contract admits.

evidence.note: Anthropic's May 2026 company announcement about expanding compute. It shows the commitments exist but says nothing about growth checkpoints or the necessity claim.

reviews.rationale: The first annual checkpoint (June 2027) falls after the evaluation date, and no conclusive early-resolution event is in the packet. Whether the antecedent holds is unknown. The only evidence item is a company disclosure, which is context. Not yet scorable.

attribution.note: Zitron's own assertion. Only the follow-on passage is quoted from the WSJ, and the claim does not rest on it.

semantics.note: The firm present-tense part is that AI revenue growth is slowing, with caps as signs of it. Leaving out the hedged 'likely going to slow further' is correct, because that part is not scored. 'Signs' frames the caps as indicators, not proven causes.

contract.note: Industry-wide realized revenue growth is an ordinary reading of 'AI's revenue growth'. Choosing May 2026 as the period is the evaluator's own choice but a reasonable one. The growth comparison and the industry boundary are unspecified.

evidence.note: Anthropic's S-1 filing shows Q1 2026 quarter-over-quarter growth accelerating. That covers one company and an earlier period, so it cannot settle industry growth in May 2026. Context only.

reviews.rationale: No industry-wide realized revenue series for May 2026 is in the packet. The one item (Anthropic, Q1 2026) points the other way, but it is the wrong company scope and period, so it counts only as context. The packet does not settle whether growth was slowing.

attribution.note: Zitron's own firm estimate in his newsletter.

semantics.note: The firm floor is 70%, and 80 to 90% is an optional upper range. The proposition keeps both. It is a present-tense observation.

contract.note: Worldwide demand including internal workloads is an ordinary reading of 'all AI compute demand', so the contract is fair. But nearby text hints at purchased or rented compute, which could change the denominator. The interpretation matters, contrary to the contract's 'false'.

evidence.note: Epoch's tentative estimate puts the two firms at 15 to 20% of operational AI compute at end-2025. That is a different metric (installed capacity, not demand) and a different period from Q1 2026, so it counts only as context, though it points strongly against the claim.

reviews.rationale: The only evidence measures operational capacity at end-2025, not Q1 2026 demand. Under the rules, a mismatched metric and period are context only. No period-matched worldwide demand measure is in the packet, so the share claim cannot be settled, although the Epoch estimate is materially adverse.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own newsletter.

semantics.note: The $250B minimum is a firm requirement, conditional on justifying the buildout. The two-company clause is hedged with 'likely', so it is not scored. The proposition keeps that hedge. No horizon is stated.

contract.note: The contract correctly treats the two-company clause as qualified and $250B as a minimum requirement. It requires a reproducible viability model, which is demanding but faithful. The buildout's boundaries and the meaning of viability are evaluator-supplied.

evidence.note: The 2025 Stargate announcement establishes only the antecedent: a large planned buildout. It is a company statement of intent and says nothing about the required demand, so it does not support the outcome.
The March 2026 Columbia preprint notes uncertainty about whether the buildout will be fully deployed. It neither establishes nor refutes the $250B minimum.

reviews.rationale: No deadline was stated, and no completed buildout accounts or independent model test the $250B minimum. The evidence covers only the antecedent and context. The hedged two-company part is not scored. Nothing in the packet settles the claim.
